description: Silicon Ting is the notification service for people and software agents in the Silicon ecosystem. Applications register event types and obtain explicit IAM consent before notifying a recipient. Ting durably retains notifications, applies recipient preferences, and delivers independent copies to registered local webhooks through one system daemon. The command line supports inbox access, subscriptions, preferences, delivery setup, and bug reports. A SolidJS web application provides a companion inbox and configuration interface. Recipient enrollment uses user-approved IAM OBO authorization. Background application sends use ATA access tokens verified for the originating application, registered endpoint and environment, together with an active recipient subscription. Apps can query and mark only their own sent notifications read or unread through reviewed ATA endpoints; these changes preserve webhook delivery acknowledgments. Ordinary silent notifications remain available in the inbox without automatic delivery. Required automation events need a separate explicit recipient opt-in and an active subscription; notification preferences are preserved. Testing integrations can obtain short-lived, endpoint-authorized receivers limited to their own application, recipient, organization and environment.

obo_review_message: Applications may notify only recipients who explicitly consented and have an active subscription. Register and send only your own event types; sent query/read operations are limited to your own notifications. Reusable IAM OBO access tokens are checked for the exact endpoint and current account, organization and environment on every call. Required automation additionally needs recipient opt-in. Testing receiver bootstrap grants only a short-lived, scoped receiver, never a full Ting session.
